- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Model often overreacts to recent price highs; apply mean reversion bias: if forecast > 20% above recent 5-day high, reduce by 10–15%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be 2–4% too high in early periods; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model fails to capture momentum; smooth forecast with weighted average of 3–5 prior days.
